meta.title: Automated Device Enrollment: Token Setup and Profile Assignment

views.label: Set up API credentials
views.note: Upload the server’s public certificate to the Apple portal, then import the encrypted server token.

views.label: Reconcile inventory and profiles
views.note: The dep workers synchronize Apple inventory and reconcile enrollment-profile assignments on repeated runs.

cards.title: Server-token setup
items: The operator uploads the public certificate and imports the encrypted .p7m server token. The retained private key decrypts the OAuth credentials; this is separate from an MDM push certificate.
Validation occurs before a locked commit. Ordinary imports reject an established Apple identity or consumer-key change; a concurrent credential or staged-key change rejects the candidate.

cards.title: Recurring reconciliation
items: Inventory starts with a full fetch, then follows incremental cursors. Invalid or expired cursors restart a fetch. Only successful completion of the current generation reconciles missing devices.
Sync and assignment have independent schedules. Assignment and admission resolve an explicit account/serial choice, the account default, then no action. Profiles coexist without selecting a default.

Serial is the physical-device selection key; UUID remains Apple’s profile identifier. Batches group serials by resolved UUID. Removing a choice resumes the default and never clears Apple’s profile implicitly.

cards.title: Caller-supplied profile checks
items: Before submission, Profile.ValidateForTarget checks explicit OS/version and capability facts against generated skip-key availability and documented ADE field restrictions. It never changes profile content or chooses a profile.

Unsupported fields, unchecked dimensions, deprecations and ignored iOS flags remain separate. Missing facts and conditional Setup Assistant panes remain unchecked; callers decide whether the evidence is sufficient.

The Apple client and reference-server assignment retain structural validation only. Target-aware validation is an explicit library operation because those paths do not have complete target capabilities.

cards.title: Retry and concurrency
items: HTTP 429 and per-device THROTTLED results defer assignments. A still-owned lease preserves cooldowns across same-identity credential renewal or a changed desired profile, even when its business result is stale.
An identity reset or lost lease rejects old cooldown writes. Account and cursor checks reject stale inventory pages; each accepted page commits atomically with its cursor.

A local conflict stops further batches. A store-owned revision fences serial/default edits, including changes away and back, and selected-definition writes. Credential, identity and lease checks also guard outcomes and readback.

Each mutation first commits PENDING uncertainty. Missing or unrecognized assignment outcomes retain it. A replacement run reads Apple’s device details before resubmission; inaccessible readback blocks retries. Confirmed success is retained without a duplicate assignment.

cards.title: Explicit identity replacement
items: Force resets state only for an actual identity change with a validated server UUID. The transaction clears old inventory, profile definitions, default and serial choices, sessions and retry state, and starts a fresh fetch generation.

The account name, protocol version, creation time and token keypairs survive. Same-identity renewals preserve inventory and all desired choices; omitted identity metadata does not erase an established binding.
SQL schema 3 locks a stable account-name row, including absent names and delete/recreate transitions. Custom stores must provide the same transaction-long LockAccount contract.

SQL schema 4 adds a replayable profile-choices table; account defaults remain in their existing column. Migration replay preserves selected profiles, credentials, keys, worker uncertainty and checkpoints.
